fields.label: Intro paragraph
fields.value: A toothache can make it difficult to eat, sleep or concentrate. Whether your pain is a dull ache, sharp sensitivity or an intense throbbing, it is your body's way of telling you something needs attention. At Precision Dental, we offer urgent appointments to find the cause of your pain and help you feel comfortable again.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Is a Toothache?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: A toothache is pain in or around a tooth. It can have many causes, including tooth decay, a cracked tooth, a lost or broken filling, gum inflammation, an infection within the tooth or an erupting wisdom tooth. Sometimes, pain felt in the teeth originates elsewhere, such as the sinuses or jaw muscles, particularly in people who grind or clench.

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The type of pain can offer clues. Brief sensitivity to cold may point to exposed dentine or early decay, while lingering pain, throbbing or pain that wakes you at night may suggest inflammation or infection of the nerve.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: When to Seek Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Please contact us promptly if you have:

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain lasting more than a day or two

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Throbbing pain or pain that keeps you awake

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Pain when biting or chewing

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Sensitivity that lingers after hot or cold food and drink

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Swelling in the gums or face

fields.label: List item
fields.value: Fever or a bad taste in your mouth

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: If you have facial swelling affecting your breathing or swallowing, or swelling spreading towards your eye or neck, call 000 or go to your nearest hospital emergency department.

sections.label: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What to Do Before Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Rinse your mouth with warm water and gently floss around the sore tooth to remove any trapped food. Take over-the-counter pain relief as directed on the packaging if it is suitable for you. A cold compress on the outside of your cheek may help. Avoid placing aspirin or other tablets directly on the gum, and avoid very hot, cold or sugary foods.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: What Happens at Your Appointment

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We ask about your pain, including when it started, what triggers it and how long it lasts. We then examine the area, perform simple sensitivity tests and take digital X-rays to identify the cause. Once we understand what is happening, we explain our findings and focus on relieving your discomfort. Depending on the cause, this may involve placing a filling, adjusting your bite, treating inflamed gums, beginning root canal therapy or managing an infection. If further care is needed, we discuss your options and costs before planning your next visit.

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Aftercare and Ongoing Care

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: After treatment, some tenderness is common for a few days. Follow any specific instructions we provide, and complete any recommended follow-up treatment so the underlying cause is fully addressed. Regular check-ups help detect decay and other concerns before they cause pain.

sections.label: Why Choose Precision Dental for Toothache

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Why Choose Precision Dental for Toothache

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We set aside time for urgent appointments and use digital X-rays and an intra-oral camera to diagnose efficiently. Our team explains the cause of your pain clearly and offers happy gas for patients who feel anxious. Free on-site parking also makes getting to us easier when you are uncomfortable.

sections.label: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Fees, Health Funds and Payment Options

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: The cost of your treatment depends on your individual needs. After your examination, we talk you through your options and the expected fees before any treatment begins. We accept most major health funds, process claims on the spot through HICAPS and are a preferred provider for {{site:preferredFunds}}. Payment plans are available through DentiCare for eligible patients, subject to terms and conditions. You can learn more on our Prices and Payment Options page.

fields.label: Small label
fields.value: FAQ

fields.label: Heading
fields.value: Frequently Asked Questions

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can a toothache go away on its own?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Sometimes pain eases temporarily, but the underlying cause often remains. Pain that disappears after being severe can indicate a nerve has died, so an assessment is still important.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Why does my toothache get worse at night?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Lying down increases blood flow to the head, which may intensify pressure and pain. There are also fewer distractions at night.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Should I go to hospital for a toothache?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Most toothaches should be seen by a dentist. Go to hospital if you have swelling affecting breathing or swallowing, a high fever or swelling spreading towards your eye or neck.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Can sinus problems cause tooth pain?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Yes. Sinus congestion can cause pain in the upper back teeth. We can help determine whether the pain is dental.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: Will I need a root canal?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: Not necessarily. Many toothaches are caused by decay or sensitivity that can be treated with a filling. We will explain the options after examining your tooth.

fields.label: Question
fields.value: How soon can I be seen?

fields.label: Paragraph
fields.value: We keep time available for urgent care and will do our best to see you on the day you call.
